reports.desc: They charged me an additional $1020 (on top of the agreed upon total) for travel time to move my belongings. We live far away from a big city. They did not tell us they were booking movers from three hours away (6-hours of travel in total). If we had known we definitely would not have used their service. The travel fee in the original agreement was $25. They said nothing about the additional travel expense. They tacked that amount on at the very end and the movers would not unload our belongings until we paid the full amount.

I received multiple adds on TikTok to join their TikTok Shop merchant program. I was deceived into sending money to cover inventory/sales of product. I believe this is an investment scam. I made the first deposit on good faith thinking it was startup costs. Every order after that became more and more expensive/requesting more money. I contacted their customer service rep about closing my store and cancelling orders and was advised that is not possible until all orders are completed. After every order was completed a new one would populate requiring more money to proceed. And never being able to close the account or their guidelines

Since October 2025, I have received over 590 unsolicited prerecorded calls promoting supposed personal loans/debt relief. I have NEVER applied for a loan, answered these calls, returned a call, or consented to these solicitations. The callers continually rotate/spoof caller-ID numbers while directing recipients to recurring callback numbers using fictitious stories. Recent messages claim I have an existing “file,” that supervisors/underwriters have reviewed it, and, often lately, that numerous employees have repeatedly tried to reach me. This caller offered unsolicited "time sensitive resolution options" to my supposedly unpaid taxes. I don't owe any taxes. Other recordings use similar fictitious personal stories and loan approvals. I have preserved numerous voicemails, screenshots, dates, caller-ID numbers and callback numbers and have reported this to the FTC numerous times. This appears to be a large-scale, persistent robocall campaign, not isolated calls.

The online store advertised a product specific to Nike and the Chicago Bears.  The product, received 4 weeks after payment was made and little follow-up from the company is a counterfeit shoe (not the Nike Air Mx 90 as advertised) and is not specific to the Chicago Bears in any way (no logo, wrong team colors, nothing that indicates Chicago as originally pictured)
Typical Scam going through trademarks and providing unsolicited services.  My phone is on the do not call list.

purchased the books on ~6/5/26 via Shop app. It was supposed to be a 1 time purchase for the books. They charged me $44.95 for books + flash cards instead of $19.99 for the books. I did not purchase the flashcards nor did i receive them. Since then, i have recurring charges (despite my account indicating no subscription) on 7/13, 8/2, 9/10, and 9/27/26. I have asked them to refund and remove my info from their system at each event but they have not replied - although i have received a refund for eveything exvept for 1 order + the flash cards from the initial order.

Website to get a free tablet you fill out with all your personal information and it wasn't a tablet they want to send you a phone I do not need a phone matter of fact all they sent me was the SIM card I called him and asked about the tablet and they can't provide a tablet false advertisement misleading and asking for my social security number which no I did not give them it's a scam then I asked him for you know what's the resolution to this they give me another phone number this trying to sell me an emergency alert thing and I'm talking to a lady she would not shut up all she had to get her spell in it was being recorded I just hung up on it I don't know how many senior citizens these people scam but it's got to be a lot

I was watching TikTok and an ad popped up saying congratulations. I’ve watched a certain amount of videos and it directed me to another page.. it then said I had so many points and I could convert it into Cash. All I needed to do is pick what card I wanted the cash deposited into. So I did and then it asked me for $20 for a one time fee and the funds would be released into my account. So unfortunately, I paid $20 and then it asked me to send them another $40. I did this through Apple Cash and then I realize this was a scam after researching it.

They are not upholding their own policies and are sending trash articles of clothing. In the photo you will see what was advertised and what was received. As well as their written policy.

reports.biz: Velvet Polley - SP David Michael Ramire Tucson, AZ
reports.desc:
We were looking to purchase Pelican brand accessories for our kayaks and their site appeared legitimate. Offering a sale price on kayak tie downs and scupper plugs. We did not receive a confirmation from the on-line sale at pelician-kayaks.com but did recieve a conformation from the Shop App ( which I am not a fan of. They dont seem to check out thier vendors.)
After a couple of weeks I tried to contact the company. No phone number listed . I attempted to email the company with the oreder number and description of what we ordered. Email bounced back as undeliverable. Contacted bank to dispute  order as fraudulent activity. Debit card was cancelled. After 3 weeks still have not received order.
I avoided the scam but had “lou” email me about a job and then Brian to call me for a screening.  Thankfully didn’t fall for it because I saw the number posted on here first.

Person called denied they were a collection agency/debt collector and said they were in fact a pre litigation company. They used employer information from 2017, an employer who was closed by the feds. I thought it was something affiliated but she want on to allege that I had $1300 unpaid bill from 2020 to Bruce furniture store. She also alleged I was mailed debt settlement and did not need to provide proof of debt. She offered an option to settle a debt directly with the store and would transfer me, she was unsuccessful and told me to call the store directly.
Not only did she deny being a debt collector she said she was going to file docs with court but did not work for a law firm, and did not know what attorney would show up. Her vernacular was also suspicious as she had a hard time reiterating what was actually happening.
I ordered dentures as seen in the advertisement and received child-like plastic teeth that looked like it belonged in a Halloween costume package.
